text: Wyrmwood Reserve, Sept. 18 — Pine marten have been reintroduced to the Wyrmwood reserve in a controlled release overseen by reserve staff and biologists, people familiar with the matter said. Eight animals, including four adults fitted with tracking collars, were released last week into the reserve’s northern conifer belt after a two-year preparation effort. The species, absent from the site for decades, is expected to help restore balance by reducing overabundant rodent populations, the people said. Early monitoring showed the animals using den boxes and moving along old stream corridors. Officials plan monthly surveys through winter to assess survival and breeding activity, according to the people familiar with the matter.
